title: Meishan Permian-Triassic boundary section (GSSP)
summary: The Meishan quarries in Changxing County, Zhejiang, expose the type section for the base of the Triassic, marked by the first appearance of the conodont Hindeodus parvus at Bed 27c. Ash layers there date the end-Permian mass extinction to about 251.94 million years ago, making it the global reference for that event.

uncertainty.note: IUGS Geoheritage gives the end-Permian extinction at 251.94 Ma. The ICS Induan page lists several older determinations and says reprocessed U-Pb suggests 252.5 Ma, with the dated ash bed slightly below the boundary.

as_recorded.value: revised processing for U-Pb ages suggest 252.5 Ma

where.modern_name: Meishan, Changxing County, Huzhou, Zhejiang, China
where.historical_name: Marine carbonate shelf of the South China block (no human geography)

paleo.plate_model: MERDITH2021 (Merdith et al. 2021, Earth-Science Reviews 214:103477) via GPlates Web Service
paleo.note: Point 31.08, 119.71 reconstructed to 252 Ma. PALEOMAP gives 17.17 N, 103.88 E.

importance.justification: Global reference section for the Permian-Triassic boundary and the best-dated record of Earth's most severe extinction.
